caption:
I am grateful to the University of Oklahoma and Southern Methodist University for providing me with more than just football. I learned life lessons from these locations that I will never forget.

It wasn’t an easy journey. I struggled with depression, faced hardship, and had times when it took everything I had just to show up. But during those difficult times, I discovered the importance of tenacity. I discovered that you develop by accepting the difficult aspects of life, and that self-belief, honesty, and consistency are the foundations of strength.

I was happy again somewhere along the way, not because everything was perfect but because I discovered who I am. I learned responsibility, resiliency, and the true meaning of manhood from this game. Every early morning, every practice, and every injury served as a lesson in self-control and purpose.

I got family from football. Friends, staff, coaches, and teammates became my brothers; they encouraged me, had faith in me, and supported me through difficult times. I will always be appreciative of the individuals I can now call family.

Every stadium had a coliseum-like atmosphere. Each snap felt well-earned. I give this game everything I have because it requires sacrifice. I work, I play, and I live this journey for those who are unable to do so as well as for myself. For those who were denied the chance, for those who were forced to leave, and for those who are still engaged in invisible battles.

I respect the game for those who are unable to do so.
I will always be grateful. Always appreciative

caption:
Jeffrey M’Ba continue d’écrire l’histoire.
Passé par Auburn, Purdue puis transféré à SMU, il a confirmé son potentiel au plus haut niveau universitaire.

Son invitation au Senior Bowl est loin d’être anodine.
C’est l’un des événements les plus suivis du processus pré-draft, où les scouts NFL regardent chaque mouvement.

Cette invitation montre une chose, il est désormais bien sur les radars NFL.

Si Jeffrey est drafté, ce serait immense.
Le seul Français drafté en NFL reste Richard Tardits en 1989, il y a plus de 30 ans. ￼
Personne formé en France n’a accompli ça depuis.

On pourrait donc assister à un moment très rare dans l’histoire du foot US, voire à une nouvelle page pour les Français en NFL.

Rendez-vous dans la nuit 31 janvier au 1er février 📺
La suite s’annonce passionnante 🏈

caption: Oh wow, writing this is really bittersweet but it must be done😭. Dear SMU, thank you for being the best place a girl could ask for. I’ve felt so much love, support, and trust from the university and staff. I never knew what this year would look like for old me, but it truly was one of the best years of my life. To my coaches, thank you for believing in me, even when I didn’t. You guys really helped me grow into the person I am today. Thank you for dealing with my defense…… and letting me get better there lol. To my teammates…I could cry…. I just love you. This group of girls was like no other. I found a family for life, and I’m leaving with best friends I hope to know forever. To the support staff, thank you for dealing with my knees ahaha and finding what works for me. Georgia I love all of our talks and rant seshes, you are my savior. And to my family who never gave up on me, and saw greatness from the beginning, thank you for being my rock. Thank you for allowing me to grow and mess up. And most of all to my mom….pause I’m crying…….. you are the reason I played this sport. I couldn’t do any of this without you. I love you and you’re my forever best friend. With my whole heart, I am leaving SMU a better athlete and more complete person. I achieved my dreams of becoming All American 🇺🇸, but even beyond that First Team! From a mid-major girl, I didn’t know it could be possible, but here we are! Shoutout to CSU Vball, for helping me reach my potential and was a huge part in my growth as a human. To all CSU and SMU staff, players, and fans, I love you! #1 out of college but #11 for the Dallas Pulse! Coming 🔜 ❤️❤️❤️

caption:
“8•24•2025 When my life changed. I love you Ma Dukes. I didn’t want to drop this, but you did a fucking great job raising us — I had to let the world know. As a man, I’ve cried day and night since 6•5•2025, and the pain still cuts deep.”

Mane I’m fucked up rn 💔 My heart is beyond broken, today I had to say goodbye to my best friend & my queen, my beautiful Ma. She was my rock, my prayer warrior, my comfort, my biggest supporter & my everything. The pain, the anger, the emotions… it’s all heavy, but I know God has called her home and she is resting safely in His arms. You gave me strength I didn’t even know I had, and you always kept me grounded when shi got rough. I’ll never never forget the way you loved me unconditionally through everything. 

I promise I’ma carry all this shit through the finish line, ‘cause I know that’s what you’d want. You raised me to be strong, to keep pushing no matter what, and you always told me when shit gets harder, that’s when I’m at my best. I can’t lie, I feel empty as hell right now, like a piece of me gone.

Damn, you’re killing me lady… I love you so much. I’d give up everything just to see you again. You were the best fighter I knew, and you showed unwavering faith every step of the way. Please watch over us, guide us, and keep protecting your family. Woman, you filled out every box in every category, never let anything break you. You stood ten toes down through it all, showing me what real strength and love look like.

Mane I’m fucked up, lost & don’t know what to do. Text can’t even describe shit like this. Ma Dukes 1 of 1 — you didn’t raise no bitch, straight soldier. The best lady I could ever ask for, couldn’t trade your love, passion, hard work & dedication for nothing. Ik you watching over us, looking down laughing like ‘y’all crazy ass,’ but still looking out for us. Your legacy lives in me, in everything I do and everything I become. This world ain’t the same without you. I got your two youngest fs. Rest easy Mama… until we meet again, I got you forever. 🕊️❤️”**

потрясающий Санкт-Петербург ❤️‍🩹
любимый город, подаривший невероятное множество возможностей. люди, которых я обрела здесь стали мне дороги, тот опыт, что я приобрела здесь-пока что самый ценный в моей жизни, первые годы абсолютно самостоятельной жизни, с какими-то вещами я столкнулась впервые, на своих ошибках я училась, но самое важное что я извлекла-это не останавливаться и продолжать делать свое дело несмотря ни на какие обстоятельства и смотреть только вперед . это был классный сезон, в котором, как я думаю, мы сами для себя показали, что нет ничего невозможного, серебро регулярки и бронза плей офф для меня точно ощущаются как золото, ведь мы преодолевали огромное количество препятствий на протяжении всего сезона и рада, что мне посчастливилось стать частью этой команды, 
я горжусь тем, какой путь мы прошли! 
и чувствую, что мне пора идти дальше 🙏🏼
благодарна всем, кто был причастен к этим 2 сезонам в Спартаке и в особенности  нашему главному тренеру, мотиватору, локомотиву и просто хорошему человеку
new chapter is getting unlocked… 🔓 
P.S. no rain - no flowers 🤍

caption:
Hey everyone… I honestly can’t believe I’m saying this, but my first single, Can’t Help But Cry, is finally dropping next week.

This moment means everything to me. It’s been such a long journey full of late nights, doubts, growth, and learning how to trust myself and my voice. This isn’t just a song release… it’s a dream I’ve been holding onto for a long time. And to be here, now, sharing it with you  it’s honestly emotional.

Can’t Help But Cry is for anyone who’s ever felt hurt, unappreciated, or stuck in emotions you couldn’t explain. It’s for the people who love hard, even when it’s not returned the way it should be. If you’ve ever held it together in front of everyone but broke down alone  this is for you.

I poured my heart into every word, every note. And I hope it brings you comfort, or even just a moment of release because I know how heavy it can feel sometimes.

Thank you to everyone who’s believed in me, supported me, or just stuck around on this journey. I’m beyond grateful.

athlete.name: Morgan Tribbett
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with an astute football IQ, this long snapper combines precision with a calm demeanor, embodying teamwork and dedication. Off the field, a spirited leader fostering camaraderie and resilience.

caption:
SMU long snapper Morgan Tribbett made the trip to Eau Claire Wisconsin to chase perfection!

Morgan and I have been working together virtually for a while now on helping him become more efficient. But it’s always great to get in person and take a deep dive into technique!

Morgan and I found that he was struggling with his dominant thumb flipping up through the snap causing his right hand to cup the ball through the release. While it wasn’t causing any glaring issues, it’s definitely another variable that we can work on eliminating to help bring even more consistency!

We spent a good chunk of time on the hands, giving him the tools to work towards perfection. We then took our attention to creating a little more length in his snap to allow for better body control. Most snappers will easily condense their movement because it is comfortable. Morgan had the same issue. Through a handful of drills and helping him mentally become more patient we were able to help him create more flow. Once we had that we spent some time on his blocking footwork! A lot of snappers have some big misconceptions when it comes to blocking as a snapper. We helped Morgan install rules to his blocking so he is able to get his body in the best position possible to take on his opponent and be an athlete!

I’m excited for the gains we made and looking forward to continuing to help Morgan chase perfection!

caption:
S1. Episode 7: Jeffrey M’ba What’s your dream? 

@j5ffrey Let me tell you MY DREAM 

Was born in Africa and I was raised in France. Only reason here in America is to play football. It was the only reason I came here and the only reason I’m still here. I want to play in the NFL be a pro bowler I wanna work with a brand and be able to have my own line and create my own clothes. 

I choose to go to SMU for my last year. Football is really the focus. I have a lot of people to prove wrong. I have a lot of things to prove to myself as well, and show the world who I am. 

Think about what you want first before thinking about saving the world. And they will come and I was showed by action. To have a big impact in the future of a lot of kids, you have to do it. You have to do things. You have to show them the way to do it. My dream is to be able to be free, to be whatever I want to be.

That’s my dream.

20.8PPG

caption:
Colorado State long snapper Morgan Tribbett made the trip to Eau Claire WI to chase perfection!

I’m very excited for Morgan. He’s a great athlete and with the right tools he can be a great long snapper as well! Morgan’s biggest issue right now is that he had a lot of inefficiencies based on how’s he’s been thinking about the snap. 

It’s very common to find inefficient coaching cues online and unfortunately they get spread often… Morgan has been doing some things with his body that are counter productive to the snap. 

During our session we focused a lot on educating about the WHY and HOW of the snap. Relating the movement to other common sports and implementing the physics that allow a successful throw or strike to happen. 

One of the biggest issues we saw with Morgan’s initial technique is that he was trying to drive the ball straight back right away while simultaneously hopping backwards in an attempt to create power. 

If you’ve ever watched anyone throw or studied basic biomechanics you would understand that the implement (the ball) never initiates the throw. Imagine a baseball player throwing the ball before he stepped toward the target. We also know that creating a block is essential to transferring energy. A block happens in EVERY throwing sport. It’s essentially the stoppage of the lower body/grounding of the lower body to allow the energy created to transfer into the ball. When this DOESNT happen, the throw tends to be slower and even less accurate. 

By simply focusing our energy on those two topics we made HUGE strides in his snapping! We dug into a lot of other topics during our time together as well, but those are probably the most incorrectly coached aspects of the snap. NEVER move the ball first. The laws of physics prove that to not be the most efficient way to snap. Stay grounded through the throw. We never want to dissipate energy as we snap!

Always chase perfection, ask questions, and you’ll see results!

Looking forward to continuing to help Morgan chase perfection!
